recovery_analysis.restructuring_framework: English Law (Bond & Intercreditor) / BVI Legal Perimeter / DIFC Arbitration
recovery_analysis.thesis: Khor Mor's essential role generating >80% of KRI electricity makes asset liquidation or state expropriation impossible without catastrophic regional blackout. Under distressed stress (ongoing drone attacks, full KRG payment freeze, and localized condensate trucking discounts), liquidation scrap and salvage value of gas processing trains, pipeline spurs, and DFC sovereign umbrella anchor a hard recovery floor of 62.0c. In consensual going-concern restructuring, 15 Tcf 2P reserves and 750 MMscfd capacity support 100c+ par recovery.

management_questions.focus_area: Federal MOE (Kirkuk) Settlement Rail & FX Trapping
management_questions.question: Under the 100 MMscf/d Kirkuk Gas Sales Agreement commenced in August 2026, what is the precise settlement currency, paying entity, and clearance channel? Are payments settled in unencumbered offshore USD through the Trade Bank of Iraq (TBI) and the NY Fed clearance window, or are funds credited in Iraqi Dinars (IQD) at the official CBI rate (1,310 IQD) subject to central bank conversion queues? If the KRG attempts to interfere with the physical valve at the border, does the MOE contract contain an enforceable sovereign take-or-pay guarantee backed by federal oil revenues?
management_questions.relevance: Determines whether the Kirkuk contract provides clean, hard-currency cash flow diversification or traps cash in local dinar banking rails.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Direct USD offshore clearance warrants High-conviction Overweight; trapped IQD requires higher spread cushion.
management_questions.deduced_from: August 2026 announcement of Kirkuk gas deliveries and public dispute with KRG Ministry of Natural Resources.

management_questions.question: With the Iraq-Turkey Pipeline (ITP) closed since March 2023, what is the exact netback clearing mechanism for Khor Mor's ~18,000 bpd of condensate? What is the current realized dollar discount to Dated Brent across your primary local buyers (e.g., KAR Group / Bazian refinery), and what percentage of this revenue is received in clean cash versus non-cash offsets against KRG power invoices or local diesel barter?
management_questions.relevance: Condensate represents the primary liquid margin generator; deep discounts directly reduce FCF conversion.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Realized discount under $18/bbl in cash supports credit rating upgrade; barter/offsets exceeding 40% flags working capital leakage.
management_questions.deduced_from: Protracted closure of ITP pipeline and domestic Kurdistan refinery marketing dynamics.

management_questions.focus_area: U.S. DFC Intercreditor Covenants & Political Violence Acceleration Triggers
management_questions.question: Under the Intercreditor Agreement governing the $250M U.S. DFC facility and the $350M 13% Nordic bond, what are the specific 'force majeure / cessation of operations' covenant triggers? Does the DFC hold unilateral acceleration or cash sweep rights if drone strikes result in an operational shut-in exceeding 30 consecutive days, and does DFC approval require a minimum debt-service coverage ratio (DSCR) before any cash dividends can be upstreamed to Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum?
management_questions.relevance: Intercreditor priority dictates whether bondholders are subordinated to sovereign DFI acceleration in a severe security crisis.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Pari passu standstill covenants protect bondholders; unilateral DFC cash sweeps create severe refinancing risk.
management_questions.deduced_from: Co-existence of $250M DFC project loan and $350M Nordic ABM bond sharing Khor Mor first-lien collateral.

management_questions.focus_area: Enerflex EPC Contract Settlement & Standby Cost Allocation
management_questions.question: Following the April 2024 fatal drone strike and Enerflex's invocation of Force Majeure and demobilization, what were the final confidential commercial settlement terms with Enerflex? How much in demobilization claims, standby fees, and contractor acceleration premiums were incurred, and were these costs capitalized into the final $1.1B project cost or expensed through the P&L?
management_questions.relevance: Reveals whether hidden contractor liabilities or contingent arbitration claims remain unresolved.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Full and final mutual release with zero residual liability secures clean balance sheet.
management_questions.deduced_from: Enerflex's public suspension of KM250 construction in April 2024 following drone strike.

management_questions.focus_area: C-RAM & Air Defense Operational Cost Allocation
management_questions.question: Following the installation of counter-drone and air defense systems at Khor Mor in late 2024/2025, how are the ongoing operational, radar maintenance, and ammunition replenishment costs allocated? Are these costs borne directly by Pearl Petroleum as operating expenses (reducing net entitlement cash flow), or are they funded under a bilateral sovereign defense agreement between the U.S. Government and the Iraqi Ministry of Defense?
management_questions.relevance: Air defense operating costs in hostile frontier environments can add millions to annual operating overhead.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Sovereign-funded military protection insulates OPEX from security inflation.
management_questions.deduced_from: Deployment of U.S. air defense systems around Khor Mor gas complex.

management_questions.focus_area: KRG Receivables Overdue Threshold & DSRA Cash Lock-Up
management_questions.question: Under the Nordic ABM bond terms (NO0013387860), what is the explicit Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) or overdue receivables dollar cap that triggers a Restricted Payments dividend lock-up? With KRG payment delays continuing on historical arrears, what proportion of Pearl's current $95M cash balance is trapped in mandatory Debt Service Reserve Accounts (DSRA) versus freely distributable cash to the joint venture partners?
management_questions.relevance: Determines true unencumbered liquidity available for bond debt service vs dividend drain.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Stringent DSRA lock-up covenants protect bondholders by trapping project cash flows.
management_questions.deduced_from: Consistently high dividend upstreams ($300M+ in 2025) despite KRG receivables arrears.

management_questions.focus_area: European Partner Governance & Exit Pre-emption Rights
management_questions.question: Given that KM250 is fully commissioned and OMV/MOL/RWE hold 10% non-operated stakes each, have any of the European partners formally signaled intentions to exercise tag-along, drag-along, or pre-emption rights to divest their stakes to regional players, and how would a change of ownership in the 30% European block impact the change-of-control put option (at 101%) in the 2028 notes?
management_questions.relevance: Potential consortium reshuffling could alter governance dynamics or trigger bond put options.
management_questions.conviction_trigger: Stable long-term partner pact preserves institutional governance credibility.
management_questions.deduced_from: European majors' ongoing portfolio rationalization in frontier non-operated hydrocarbon assets.

credit_view.desk_thesis: Pearl Petroleum represents one of the most profitable, low-cost upstream gas assets in CEEMEA, producing over 80% of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq's (KRI) electricity fuel from the world-class Khor Mor field (>15 Tcf 2P gas reserves). The operational risk profile has fundamentally de-risked following the completion of the $1.1B KM250 expansion, boosting nameplate processing capacity by 50% from 500 MMscfd to 750 MMscfd, with production ramped past 70,000 boepd. Financial leverage is exceptionally conservative at ~1.0x Net Debt / EBITDA ($595M Gross Debt, $95M Cash, ~$500M LTM EBITDA). Credit risks are strictly political, security, and counterparty-driven rather than operational or structural insolvency: (1) Khor Mor has suffered repeated drone strikes by pro-Iranian PMF militias (mitigated by newly installed U.S. C-RAM air defenses); (2) the KRG remains in multi-year arrears on payment tranches; and (3) Pearl's bold decision to bypass Erbil and pipe 100 MMscfd directly to the Iraqi Federal Ministry of Electricity in Kirkuk (started August 2026) has triggered contractual pushback from the KRG, but provides an indispensable direct USD payment rail from Baghdad. At 103.5¢ (~11.5% YTM) with senior first-lien security shared with the U.S. DFC, the 13% coupon provides exceptional carry cushion against regional geopolitical volatility.
positives: Unassailable Domestic Electricity Moat: Supplies over 80% of natural gas for power generation across the KRI (Bazian, Erbil, Chemchemal). Physical shut-down or expropriation is impossible without instant regional blackout.
World-Class Reserve Life & Ultra-Low Lifting Cost: 15.2 Tcf gas and 510 mmbbl liquids (gross 2P). Operating costs under $2.50/boe generate >80% EBITDA margins.
Successful KM250 Commissioning: Expansion completed, taking capacity from 500 MMscfd to 750 MMscfd and ramping gross production past 70,000 boepd.
Conservative Balance Sheet: Net debt of $500M against ~$510M EBITDA (0.98x net leverage) with $95M cash buffer and 7.2x interest coverage.
U.S. DFC Sovereign Anchor: $250M U.S. DFC facility aligns Washington's geopolitical interest with asset protection, leading directly to U.S. C-RAM counter-drone deployment.
negatives: KRG Structural Payment Arrears: KRG remains in multi-year payment arrears following the March 2023 closure of the Iraq-Turkey Pipeline (ITP).
Asymmetric Drone & Rocket Strikes: Field repeatedly targeted by pro-Iranian PMF militias in Kirkuk/Taza (lethal strike in April 2024 killed 4 contractors).
Kirkuk Gas Sales Contractual Friction: August 2026 supply of 100 MMscfd to Federal Iraq MOE sparked claims of contractual breach from KRG Ministry of Natural Resources.
Local Condensate Discounting: ITP closure forces ~18,000 bpd of condensate into local refinery trucking at steep $20–$25/bbl discounts to Dated Brent.
Aggressive Upstream Dividend Leakage: High dividend payouts to Dana Gas ($105M) and Crescent Petroleum ($105M) drain liquidity rather than pre-funding May 2028 bond bullet repayment.
credit_view.background: Pearl Petroleum Company Limited is a five-member consortium founded in 2007 by Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum (35% each, joint operators), joined in 2009 by OMV (10%) and MOL Group (10%), and in 2015 by RWE (10%). The consortium holds 100% of the Petroleum Development Agreement covering the Khor Mor and Chemchemal gas fields in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Khor Mor is the largest non-associated gas field in Iraq outside federal control, holding 15.2 Tcf of 2P gas reserves.
credit_view.recent_drivers: Completion of the $1.1B KM250 expansion in late 2025 / early 2026 increased gas processing capacity by 50% to 750 MMscfd. In August 2026, Pearl commenced direct gas deliveries of 100 MMscfd to the Federal Ministry of Electricity at the Taza power plant in Kirkuk. 1H26 collections reached $104M (Dana Gas 35% share) and Pearl holds $95M in unrestricted cash.

historical_notes.title: Comprehensive Credit Assessment: KM250 Commercial Ramp, 13% 2028 Senior Secured Bond & Geopolitical Risk Review
historical_notes.author: Institutional Buy-Side Credit Desk; CEEMEA Energy & Special Situations
historical_notes.source: Consortium Disclosures, Dana Gas 1H26 Financials & Nordic ABM Regulatory Filings
historical_notes.full_note:
PEARL PETROLEUM COMPANY LIMITED — COMPREHENSIVE CREDIT REVIEW & CAPITAL STRUCTURE ASSESSMENT

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & DESK VERDICT:
We initiate coverage on Pearl Petroleum Company Limited with an OVERWEIGHT / SECURED CARRY stance on the PEARL 13.00% Senior Secured Notes due May 15, 2028 (ISIN: NO0013387860), trading at ~103.50¢ for an 11.45% Yield to Maturity (+625 bps spread vs UST). Pearl operates the giant Khor Mor and Chemchemal gas fields in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), producing over 80% of the region's electricity fuel. The commissioning of the $1.1B KM250 expansion has successfully de-risked the operational profile, boosting processing capacity from 500 MMscfd to 750 MMscfd and lifting gross production above 70,000 boepd. Financial leverage is exceptionally conservative at ~1.0x Net Debt / EBITDA ($595M Gross Debt, $95M Cash, ~$510M LTM EBITDA). The 13.00% coupon carry provides robust total return insulation against regional geopolitical and payment friction.

2. ASSET MOAT & OPERATIONAL REALITY:
• Khor Mor Concession: Holds 15.2 Tcf of 2P natural gas reserves and 510 mmbbl of liquids. Consortium owned 35% Dana Gas, 35% Crescent Petroleum, 10% OMV, 10% MOL, 10% RWE.
• Lifting Economics: Unit lifting cost is remarkably low at <$2.50/boe, generating massive gross cash flow margins (>80% EBITDA margin).
• KM250 Milestone: Oct-2025 commissioning added 250 MMscfd capacity, expanding output to 655 MMscfd dedicated to KRG power stations (Bazian, Erbil, Chemchemal) and 100 MMscfd to Federal Iraq.
• The Kirkuk Gas Diversion (August 2026): Pearl commenced supplying 100 MMscfd directly to the Iraqi Federal Ministry of Electricity at the Taza power plant in Kirkuk under a 1-year GSA. Despite KRG objections regarding authorization, this pivot establishes a vital hard-currency payment rail directly from Baghdad, hedging Erbil payment arrears.

3. CAPITAL STRUCTURE & DEBT INSTRUMENTS:
• $350.0M Senior Secured 13.00% Notes due 15-May-2028 (NO0013387860): Listed on Nordic ABM. First-lien pledge over Pearl shares, collection bank accounts, and Khor Mor plant assets. Traded price 103.5¢ (11.45% YTM).
• $185.0M U.S. DFC Project Finance Loan: 7-year term facility amortizing through 2028, senior secured pari passu with bond.
• $60.0M Regional Commercial Bank Tranches: Working capital lines from Bank of Sharjah syndicate.
• Gross Debt: $595.0M | Cash: $95.0M | Net Debt: $500.0M | Net Leverage: 0.98x | Gross Leverage: 1.17x | Interest Coverage: 7.2x.

4. KEY CREDIT RISKS & MITIGANTS:
• Counterparty Arrears: KRG payment delays persist (>3 years on legacy tranches) due to the shutdown of the Iraq-Turkey Pipeline (ITP). Mitigated by KRG's absolute dependence on Khor Mor fuel to avoid regional electrical collapse, plus newly established Federal Iraq cash flows.
• Geopolitical Drone Threat: Targeted repeatedly by pro-Iranian militias in Kirkuk/Taza (April 2024 lethal attack). Mitigated by newly deployed U.S. C-RAM counter-drone air defense systems.
• Condensate Discounting: Inability to pipe condensate to Ceyhan forces local trucking to domestic refiners at $20-$25/bbl discounts to Brent. Compensated by 50% expansion in gas throughput.
• Dividend Leakage: Over $300M in HoldCo dividend upstreams in 2025. Bondholders are protected by 1.75x net leverage gateway and DSRA reserve requirements.

5. DESK CONCLUSION:
Pearl's credit risk is defined by geopolitical and counterparty factors rather than balance sheet insolvency. With 1.0x net leverage, first-lien asset security, U.S. DFC co-lending protection, and an irreplaceable domestic power monopoly, PEARL 2028s at 103.5¢ (~11.5% YTM) represent an outstanding risk-adjusted carry opportunity in CEEMEA energy.
